correctness.rationale: For each rectangular poset the two-variable recursively rebinding formula H_t(z) exactly detects rank at least t. The maximum rank \(h=m+n-2\) is thus definable by FO2 sentences. In a nonchain, all rank-one elements are precisely the two coordinate atoms; points incomparable with each atom are exactly points on the opposite nonzero axis, with ranks respectively 1..n-1 and 1..m-1. The largest t with E_t true is max(m,n)-1, yielding m,n from h,t, and this also handles one-chain-factor boundary cases. Unordered equal factors give coordinate-swap isomorphisms. With only one variable the only order atom x<=x is tautological on the class; hence FO1 collapse. The explicit sentence construction gives quantifier rank <=max(h,hprime)+3. Standalone check 1 tested 324 ordered parameter pairs and 1,877,922 ordered incomparable pairs; separate noncounting FO2 type refinement split all 45 unordered rectangles with factors <=9. Finite calculations corroborate, not substitute for symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: The exact unrestricted FO2 equivalence of finite two-factor chain products in a single coordinatewise partial order, with reconstruction via atom-incomparability rank spectra, was not implied by the inspected published results. The 2012 Schwentick--Zeume paper studies satisfiability/complexity for two named order relations, not identifying lengths using the single coordinatewise order; the 2013 Manuel--Zeume paper studies two-order and successor enriched data-word structures, likewise not a same-signature identification theorem. The 2026 Marzec--Tendera general partial-order work addresses satisfiability fragments and is not a universal rectangular identification result. Cambridge finite-poset text describes products of chains as distributive lattices but not restricted-variable logical identification. No retrieved published research index record established this unrestricted two-variable theorem, including comparison with nearby finite-rank results; this absence is not a proof of historical novelty.

value.rationale: A complete infinite-family classification for the minimal possible nontrivial variable width in an intentionally weak natural lattice signature. It is mathematically substantive that FO2, despite lacking definable cover, meet, join, coordinates or counting quantifiers, recognizes both arbitrarily large chain lengths through the rank-one incomparability spectrum. The variable-width boundary is sharp (one variable collapses all members, two separates all) and the explicit depth bound supplies reproducible logical witnesses. This advances beyond a finite sample and motivates finer questions for product posets with three or more factors; it is not merely the ordinary order-isomorphism classification.
